text: It's important because at the end of the day, it is those business critical outcomes against which you and your team will be evaluated. That's the reality of working for a business, right?
speaker: Matt LeMay
context: Lenny asks Matt why aligning work to business critical outcomes is so important. Matt explains that product managers and teams are increasingly being laid off, and CEOs are explicitly stating they have 'too many teams doing work around the work' rather than focusing on real impact. Matt emphasizes that teams will ultimately be evaluated based on their contribution to business critical outcomes, not on following best practices or shipping features.
text_ko: 중요한 이유는 결국 여러분과 팀이 비즈니스 핵심 성과(business critical outcomes)를 기준으로 평가받기 때문이에요. 그게 회사에서 일하는 현실이죠, 맞아요?
text_zh: 关键在于，归根结底，你和团队最终会拿那些对业务最关键的结果（business-critical outcomes）来考核你们。在公司工作的现实就是这样，对吧？
text_es: Es importante porque, al final del día, son esos resultados clave para el negocio (business critical outcomes) en función de los cuales usted y su equipo serán evaluados. Esa es la realidad de trabajar en una empresa, ¿verdad?
key_sentence: it is those business critical outcomes against which you and your team will be evaluated.
original_text: It's important because at the end of the day, it is those business critical outcomes against which you and your team will be evaluated. That's the reality of working for a business, right? If you are contributing to the business in a way that the business at large can understand, that the CEO can understand, that the CFO can understand, if your team is a good investment for the business, then the business will continue making that investment.

vocabulary.definition: Referring to elements, processes, or outcomes that are essential for the survival and success of a business.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, identifying business critical factors helps prioritize resources and efforts to ensure operational continuity and strategic goals are met.
vocabulary.nuance: This term often carries a sense of urgency and importance, indicating that failure to address these factors could lead to significant negative consequences.

vocabulary.definition: To assess or appraise the value, quality, or performance of something based on specific criteria.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, employees and projects are frequently evaluated to determine effectiveness, efficiency, and alignment with organizational goals.
vocabulary.nuance: The term suggests a formal process of judgment, often involving metrics or standards, rather than informal or subjective opinions.

vocabulary.definition: The results or consequences of actions, decisions, or processes within a business context.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, outcomes are often measured to evaluate the success of strategies, projects, or initiatives against predefined goals.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can imply both positive and negative results, and is often used in discussions about performance metrics and accountability.

text: We still have too many teams doing work around the work and supporting work, rather than focusing on opportunities with real impact.
speaker: Matt LeMay
context: Lenny asks what this focus on business impact is a reaction to, wondering why many product teams aren't already driving business impact. Matt explains that more product managers and teams are being laid off, citing a specific example from Spotify's CEO Daniel Ek who explicitly stated the problem: too many teams doing 'work around the work' instead of focusing on real impact.
text_ko: 아직도 너무 많은 팀이 실제 영향력이 있는 기회(opportunities with real impact)에 집중하기보다 업무를 둘러싼 잡무(work around the work)나 지원 업무(supporting work)를 처리하느라 바빠요.
text_zh: 我们还有太多团队忙着做周边或支持性的事情，没把重心放在能带来真正影响的机会上。
text_es: Todavía tenemos demasiados equipos ocupados en tareas periféricas y de apoyo, en vez de centrarse en oportunidades que tengan un impacto real.
key_sentence: focusing on opportunities with real impact.
original_text: The message that Daniel Ek from Spotify sent out with their layoffs in 2024 said, 'We still have too many teams doing work around the work and supporting work, rather than focusing on opportunities with real impact.' And that really struck a nerve because I've been on those supporting teams before. I've done the work around the work.

vocabulary.definition: A significant effect or influence that leads to measurable change or improvement.
vocabulary.businessContext: In corporate discussions, 'real impact' often refers to outcomes that contribute to the bottom line, enhance customer satisfaction, or drive strategic goals.
vocabulary.nuance: The term suggests a distinction between superficial changes and those that are genuinely transformative or beneficial.

vocabulary.definition: Tasks or activities that assist or enable primary functions but do not directly contribute to core objectives.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business environment, supporting work may include administrative tasks, maintenance activities, or ancillary services that facilitate the main operations.
vocabulary.nuance: While necessary, supporting work can sometimes be viewed as secondary or less valuable compared to primary initiatives.

text: So the first question I ask most of the teams I work with is if you were the CEO of this company, would you fully fund your own team?
speaker: Matt LeMay
context: Lenny asks for ways product managers can stress test whether they're actually driving impact or just think they are. Matt shares his go-to question for teams he works with: asking them to think like a CEO and consider whether they would fully fund their own team. He notes that most people can't answer this confidently, which indicates they may not understand their team's true value to the business.
text_ko: 그래서 제가 함께 일하는 대부분의 팀에게 가장 먼저 묻는 질문은, 만약 여러분이 이 회사의 CEO라면 자신의 팀에 전폭적으로 자금을 지원하시겠어요?
text_zh: 我跟大多数团队聊的时候，问的第一个问题是：如果你是这家公司的首席执行官(CEO)，你会为自己的团队提供充足的资金支持吗？
text_es: Lo primero que pregunto a la mayoría de los equipos con los que trabajo es: si fueras director general (CEO) de esta empresa, ¿financiarías por completo a tu equipo?
key_sentence: if you were the CEO of this company, would you fully fund your own team?
original_text: So the first question I ask most of the teams I work with is if you were the CEO of this company, would you fully fund your own team? And frankly, most of the people I ask that question to don't know the answer right away. They're not sure. They say, 'I think so,' or, 'Yeah, yeah. Yeah, because...' And then you can see the gears turning.

vocabulary.definition: To provide complete financial resources necessary for a project or initiative.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, 'fully fund' often refers to allocating the total budget required to ensure a team's or project's success without any financial shortfall.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase implies a commitment to support and invest in a team or project, suggesting that partial funding may not be sufficient for achieving desired outcomes.

text: The Low Impact Death Spiral is the dynamic in which every medium to large company I've ever worked with finds itself in one way or another. It starts with teams taking on low impact work.
speaker: Matt LeMay
context: Lenny asks Matt to explain the 'Low Impact PM Death Spiral' concept from his book. Matt describes this as a common dynamic where product teams gravitate toward low-risk, low-impact work like small features and cosmetic improvements because it's safer and invites less scrutiny. This creates a cycle where low-impact work makes it harder to do high-impact work, leading teams deeper into irrelevant projects until layoffs occur.
text_ko: 낮은 영향력의 악순환(Low Impact Death Spiral)은 제가 일해 본 모든 중견·대기업이 크든 작든 어떻게든 빠지게 되는 현상이에요. 보통은 팀들이 영향이 적은 업무(low-impact work)를 맡기 시작하면서 시작돼요.
text_zh: 我把它叫做“低影响恶性循环”(Low Impact Death Spiral)。几乎我接触过的每家中大型公司都会以某种方式陷入这种状况。它通常从团队接手一些影响不大的工作开始。
text_es: La espiral de muerte por bajo impacto (Low Impact Death Spiral) es la dinámica en la que, de una u otra manera, acaba metiéndose toda empresa mediana o grande con la que he trabajado. Comienza cuando los equipos empiezan a asumir tareas que generan poco impacto.
key_sentence: The death spiral begins with teams taking on low impact work.
original_text: The Low Impact Death Spiral is the dynamic in which every medium to large company I've ever worked with finds itself in one way or another. It starts with teams taking on low impact work. Adding little features here and there, making little cosmetic improvements because it's easier, it invites less scrutiny and you're less likely to mess up something important.

vocabulary.definition: Characterized by constant change, activity, or progress; energetic and forceful.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'dynamic' often refers to the evolving nature of markets, teams, or strategies that require adaptability and responsiveness to new challenges.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'dynamic' generally has a positive connotation, it can imply unpredictability or instability in certain contexts.

vocabulary.definition: The strong effect or influence that something has on a situation, person, or process.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, 'impact' is often used to measure the effectiveness of initiatives, strategies, or changes on performance and outcomes.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can imply both positive and negative effects, so it is important to clarify the nature of the impact being discussed.

vocabulary.definition: An organization that typically employs a significant number of people and generates substantial revenue, falling between small businesses and large corporations in size and scale.
vocabulary.businessContext: This classification is important in business for understanding market dynamics, resource allocation, and strategic planning, as medium to large companies often face different challenges compared to smaller firms.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can vary in definition based on industry standards and geographical context, so it is essential to clarify the specific metrics used to define 'medium' and 'large.'

text: if your company goes out of business, they're not going to say, 'Yeah, we're going out of business, but we're going to keep writing your paycheck for two years...
speaker: Matt LeMay
context: Matt discusses the emotional challenge of being accountable for things outside our control, like business impact that depends on market conditions and customer behavior. He explains that while we naturally want to avoid accountability for uncontrollable factors, the reality is that business success affects us regardless. He uses this example to illustrate that following best practices doesn't protect you if the business fails.
text_ko: 회사가 망하면 '네, 문 닫지만 앞으로 2년 동안 월급은 계속 지급해 드릴게요'라고 말하진 않을 거예요.
text_zh: 要是你公司倒闭了，他们才不会说：“我们要倒闭了，但我们会继续给你发两年工资……”
text_es: Si tu empresa quiebra, no te van a decir: "Sí, vamos a cerrar, pero te vamos a seguir pagando el sueldo durante dos años..."
key_sentence: They won't keep writing your paycheck if the company goes out of business.
original_text: You can follow all the best practices and have the highest velocity and do everything quote-unquote 'right', but if your company goes out of business, they're not going to say, 'Yeah, we're going out of business, but we're going to keep writing your paycheck for two years because all of your OKRs were a 0.6 or a 0.7.'

text: So the first step, and I think the most important and where a lot of my work plays out is in setting team goals, close to company goals. No more than one step away from company goals. Don't let it get cascaded into oblivion.
speaker: Matt LeMay
context: Lenny asks about Matt's three steps to become more of an impact-first product team. Matt explains the first and most critical step: setting team goals that are no more than one step away from company goals. He references Christina Wodtke's concept from 'Radical Focus' about avoiding multi-level goal cascading that leads to team goals that can't be traced back to company objectives.
text_ko: 그래서 첫 번째 단계이자 제가 가장 중요하다고 생각하는 건 팀 목표를 회사 목표에 최대한 가깝게, 즉 회사 목표에서 한 단계 이내로 설정하는 거예요. 목표가 하향식으로 전파(cascade)되면서 흐지부지해지지 않도록 하세요.
text_zh: 所以第一步，也是我觉得最关键的一步，也是我大部分工作重点，就是设定团队目标，要跟公司目标紧密挂钩。最多只能偏离公司目标一步，千万别让目标在层层传递中变得面目全非。
text_es: Entonces el primer paso, y creo que es el más importante y donde se concentra gran parte de mi trabajo, es definir objetivos de equipo que estén muy alineados con los objetivos de la empresa. Como máximo un escalón por debajo de los objetivos corporativos. No dejes que se diluyan pasando de nivel en nivel hasta que no signifiquen nada.
key_sentence: Team goals must be close to company goals, not cascaded into oblivion.

vocabulary.definition: The process of establishing specific, measurable objectives for a group to achieve within a defined timeframe.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, setting team goals aligns the team's efforts with the broader organizational objectives, ensuring that all members are working towards a common purpose.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase emphasizes the collaborative nature of goal-setting and is often used to foster teamwork and accountability.

vocabulary.definition: The process of distributing information or objectives from higher levels of an organization to lower levels in a structured manner.
vocabulary.businessContext: In corporate environments, goals and strategies are often cascaded down from executives to managers and teams to ensure alignment and clarity throughout the organization.
vocabulary.nuance: While cascading can enhance communication, it may also imply a dilution of original intent if not managed properly.
